6-52 weeks: Recovery; at higher doses, prolonged erythema; permanent partial epilation
>40 weeks: Recovery; at higher doses, dermal atrophy or induration

2-8 weeks: Erythema, epilation; possible dry or moist desquamation; recovery from desquamation
>40 weeks: Telangiectasiab; or induration; skin likely to be weak

<2 weeks: Transient erythema; after very high doses, edema and acute ulceration; long-term surgical intervention likely to be required
6-52 weeks: Dermal atrophy; secondary ulceration due to failure of moist desquamation to heal; surgical intervention likely to be required; at higher doses, dermal necrosis, surgical intervention likely to be required
>40 weeks: Telangiectasiab; dermal atrophy or induration; possible late skin breakdown; wound might be persistent and progress into a deeper lesion; surgical intervention likely to be required
